text:
maria gonzalez: Quick Q — we're working on the cost dashboard CTA for chargebacks. How should we display cache savings that are shared across routes? Do we attribute to the invoking route, the prefetching route, or split?

ben liu: Short answer: split, but we need a deterministic rule.

sasha nguyen: +1 split. otherwise teams will game routing to hoard savings.

oliver park: How granular do we want to go? Per-invocation split vs. epochal amortization across a time window?

maria gonzalez: Thinking per-invocation is noisy. Proposal: amortize prefetch/cache credits over a 24h window and surface both "apportioned savings" and "direct savings" in the UI.

ben liu: That sounds reasonable. For telemetry we can emit one of two tags on requests: `cache_direct=true` or `cache_amortized_id=<uuid>` so backend can aggregate. Example event: `{"request_id":"r_123","route":"/summarize","cache_direct":false,"cache_amortized_id":"am_456"}`

amy_devrel: UX note: show a single number in default view (net token cost) and an expandable breakdown that shows amortized vs direct and the contributing routes. Keeps the main dashboard simple.

oliver park: Implementation caveat: when we split, we need to avoid double-counting on rollback/rollout windows. Canary traffic might flip at midnight and skew the amortization. Maybe attach a `rollout_tag` so we can exclude short-lived IDs (<1hr).

sasha nguyen: Agree. Add heuristic: ignore amortized IDs with total lifetime < 3600s. Also keep a sampling flag to avoid blowing up cardinality.

ben liu: Pseudo: 
```
emit_event({
  request_id, route, cost_tokens, cache_hit, amort_id, sample_rate
})
```
amortization pipeline will join on `amort_id` and produce credits per route by weight = tokens_saved_per_invocation / total_saved_for_amort_id.

cost-bot: FYI — existing billing pipeline expects `customer_tag` and `model_sku`. Please keep those in the emitted events or we'll lose joins.

maria gonzalez: Good catch — include `customer_id`, `model_sku`, and `region`. We'll also add `sampling_bucket` to make downstream sampling deterministic.

amy_devrel: Can we show a UI affordance that explains the amortization algorithm? e.g., tooltip: "Shared cache savings are spread over 24h proportional to observed token savings; ephemeral prefetches under 1hr are ignored." Helps SAs explain to customers.

oliver park: Ops question — how expensive will the join be? If `amort_id` cardinality spikes, we may OOM the aggregator. I suggest a TTL-based combiner (streaming window) and a fallback to stable median split when we hit memory pressure.

ben liu: Perf plan: 1) streaming combiner with 1h tumbling window + 24h finalization job, 2) fail-open behaviour: if combiner overloaded, write raw events to blob store and do batch amortization offline (coarser).

maria gonzalez: For the dashboard API shape, product wants endpoints: `/v1/costs/net?start=&end=&group_by=route|team|model` and `/v1/costs/credits?amortized=true|false`. Thoughts?

sasha nguyen: Solid. Also expose `explain=true` to surface how a number was computed (list of contributing amort_ids + weights). That will help debug disputes.

amy_devrel: +1 `explain` flag. Also let's add a small CSV export for finance.

oliver park: Rollout strategy: flag behind `feature.cost_amortization_v2`, enable for internal tenants, run for 2 weeks, validate parity with old rollout. If delta > 2% or any negative invoices -> rollback.

ben liu: I'll sketch event schema + aggregator proto and post a PR.

maria gonzalez: Action items: @ben draft schema & combiner plan, @oliver perf safety and TTL fallback, @amy add UX tooltip copy and export hook, @sasha add explain API surface. We'll sync tomorrow 10am. Thanks. :tada:

cost-bot: Deployment note: canary build 2026-03-19T22:14 applied to `redwood-internal` with flag `cost_amortization_v2=false`.

maria gonzalez: Great catch. Meeting invite sent.
